summary: The note covers VirtuosoTech's Holodeck Reality System (HRS), an immersive room-based technology combining VR, AR, room-scale tracking, projection mapping and haptic feedback. It describes the Tactile Mesh haptic material and applications in education, social interaction, therapy and accessibility. The article presents the HRS as a new frontier of human experience as centers open and home systems enter beta testing.
one_line: VirtuosoTech's Holodeck Reality System offers immersive, tactile virtual environments with uses in education, therapy, socializing and accessibility.
key_facts: The Holodeck Reality System (HRS) was developed by a team at VirtuosoTech, a company known for pushing the limits of digital experiences.
VirtuosoTech CEO Dr. Lia Song unveiled the HRS at a press conference, with the note giving the date as September 15, 2023.
The HRS combines next-gen VR, AR, room-scale tracking, projection mapping, and a haptic feedback system, without the cumbersome headgear and controllers of classical VR.
On October 20, 2023, VirtuosoTech revealed the 'Tactile Mesh', a 'second skin' material that gives precise haptic feedback such as wind, handshake pressure and surface textures.
Dr. Eliot Chen, lead designer of Tactile Mesh, described it as "touching the canvas of a world crafted by your imagination".
Annabelle Rosario, a former game designer turned Holodeck Reality architect, said the team is curating experiences from historical walkthroughs and life skills simulation to therapeutic settings.
On September 28, 2023, the 'Classroom of Tomorrow' initiative was announced, a collaboration between VirtuosoTech and several international educational bodies.
Social analyst Jerome Watkins said feeling physically present with someone across the globe is transformative and could become the 'new normal' for hangouts, work meetings and family gatherings.
Dr. Katrina Nguyen, a psychologist specializing in anxiety disorders, said holodecks allow exposure therapy 'without the unpredictability of the real world'.
VirtuosoTech launched the 'Access for All' program to tailor Holodeck experiences for people with disabilities.
The first HRS center, with enhanced accessibility options, opened on November 3, 2023.
By the end of the year, numerous HRS centers are expected to open and home systems are being beta tested.
